criteria.name: Story arc & swipe momentum
criteria.notes: Clear beats. 02 pays the cover at once ('Certainly possible.' plus the 42-tick gold tape). 05 to 06 and 07 to 08 pull hard. 08 is a real keepable. The bookend now partly lands: 09's blank tag is visible again at upper right on the thumb, and a small gold ribbon tail shows at the book's near corner, a quiet payoff of 08's tease. Still weak: 03 to 04 has no plant, and 04 is a 9-word frame whose object is still a blank card, so it stays the likely bail point. Seven of nine frames share one template (type on top, object below).

criteria.name: Artwork craft & genuine detail
criteria.notes: Round 5 fixed real defects. The full-width seam is gone from 03, 04 and 05: on 03 the litter now falls smoothly into the night under the body. 03's flags now print as lit paper with tooth and short casts. 05's strips carry a lit arris and lee edge, and the sphagnum falls off with the pool. 09's tag is visible again, and a gold ribbon tail exists. The strong frames are still strong: 01 (GPU PBR, thin lens, contact-probed lath), 02 (cupped gold tape, riveted hook, rimed moss), 08 (gutter valley, page stacks, satin ribbon with its cast) and 03. What holds the score under 8: 04's largest object is a blank, untextured grey gradient with no paper tooth and no crease highlight, over a dead dark band (about design y 330 to 520). Its needle ice shows diagonal moire in the far field and stair-stepped dark streaks from the 1.5x upscale. 06's litter is still bean-like ovals with no serration or midrib, each with a misregistered outline ring, and the ground hatch overprints the far trunk bases. 09's book is still a near-uniform slate slab: its page block reads as a grey board edge, not cream, and the ribbon tail is a flat pale-yellow sliver. 07's stack still reads as a white block with a seam at thumb (a refrigerator).

editor_notes_for_email: This is an update of No.88 (October 16th) and the fourth deck on the Houston land transfer, after Nos.68, 85 and 88. The news since No.88 is the October 22nd lawsuit and Crowther's October 26th testimony. Everything Crowther said on October 26th comes from ADN's account, because no legislative video or minutes could be reached, and only 'certainly possible' and 'the governor's priority' are his own words. The slides say 'per ADN' and the caption doesn't, so credit ADN if a reply quotes him. The October 8th 'AIDEA names no tenant' row on slide 08 is KTUU's paraphrase of Ruaro, not a direct quote. The case number on slide 03 was hand-filled on a scanned filing posted on plaintiff David Eastman's own website, so it is printed small, and its faintest point measures below 4.5 to 1 even though it reads at full size. The deck takes no side on the transfer, the suit or the candidates, eight days before the election. The run used all five revision rounds, and the fifth was the craft cycle. That cycle removed the horizontal seam on slides 03 to 05, made the flags on 03 read as paper and put an edge highlight on the strips on 05. On 09 it made the blank tag visible again and added a small gold ribbon. Artwork still scores 7.5, under the 8.5 craft floor, and because the cap is reached it ships as a known shortfall. The weakest frame is slide 04, whose summons is a blank grey folded card with no paper texture. The others are the bean-shaped leaves on 06 and the plain slate book on 09, whose ribbon is easy to miss at feed size. The deck scores 8.79 against this round's threshold of 7.7.
